title: First-Class Appendices for Print Reports and Zwischenbericht Anhänge
description: Add first-class appendix support to the semio print system (print/tex/): an appendix is a document attached to the main report, behaving like a chapter — numbered A, B, C…, labeled Anhang/Appendix, TOC entry, chip styling, cross-referenceable via \appendixref, listed via \listofappendices. Fix a pre-existing bug where window registers (\listoffigures etc.) render header-only because semio@render@register reads the wrong body macro. Wire the feature into all six print templates (report, paper, flyer n/a, zukunftbau forschungsbericht/zwischenbericht/kompaktbericht). Then apply it to mit-bestand/bericht/zwischenbericht/zwischenbericht.tex: convert 9 Anhang markdown documents from temp/ into 8 LaTeX appendices (A-H), including a 67-project table with per-row avatar images sourced from temp/projekt_bilder/ (downscaled ~600px, copied into zwischenbericht/asset/projekt/). Update body cross-references to use \appendixref. Full plan at /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/print-reports-should-be-joyful-haven.md.
summary:
Made table font size adjustable via a `text-size` keyval, matching the existing window option, and used it to fix the reported overflow in the zwischenbericht's Projekte and Bauteilbörsen tables.

**Adjustable table size** (semio-table.sty): added `\l_semio_table_textsize_dim`/`bool`, a `semio/table` keys_define with a `text-size` key, and `\semio@table@fontsize@apply` with 3-way precedence (explicit table option > enclosing window's `text-size` > the fixed 9.6pt chrome default). Replaced the 3 hardcoded `\fontsize{\semio@chrome@font@body}...` call sites with it. Gave `\SemioTableLong` a real optional argument — `\SemioTableLong[text-size=8pt]{title}{weights}{header}{body}` — using the kernel's own `\newcommand[5][]` optional-arg mechanism (not xparse/ltcmd, which the file's existing "Misplaced \omit" caveat rules out for macros whose body contains `\multicolumn` band rows).

**Two pre-existing bugs fixed alongside it**: `\semio_window_textsize_apply:` (semio-window.sty) wrapped its `\fontsize...\selectfont` in a group that discarded the change before any content rendered — `text-size=` on Table/Figure/Window has likely never visually applied to body text until now; fixed by dropping the pointless group. Also attempted to fix the short-table path running `\semio@table@setup` (em-based `\tabcolsep`/struts) before the font size was applied, so those metrics didn't track a custom size — **reverted after it reproducibly broke the zukunftbau `zwischenbericht` type** with a "Misplaced \omit" deep inside hhline (bisected via isolated tectonic reproductions: neither the new fontsize-apply function alone, nor `appendix-level=part` alone on a plain `semio` document, reproduce it — only relocating `\semio@table@setup` inside the same group as the tabular, specifically under that class's appendix chain, does). Left `\semio@table@setup` in its original position for `\semio@table@render`/`\SemioTableBegin`, with a comment recording why — the long-table path (used by every `SemioTableLong`, i.e. everything the overflow fix touches) was never affected, since it was already correctly ordered.

**Fixed the reported overflow** in `anhang/projekte.tex` (Katalog + Quellen tables) and 8 of 9 `SemioTableLong` tables in `anhang/bauteilboersen.tex` (all but the already-wide 2-column "Begriffe" table) with `[text-size=8pt]`. Root cause wasn't LaTeX-warned overflow (zero `Overfull \hbox … in alignment` warnings exist anywhere) — the design uses zero-gutter columns (`@{}` between cells, no vertical rules), so any cell whose text nearly fills its fixed-width column visually merges into its neighbor with no warning. Confirmed via rendered-page crops: the Katalog header row went from "Bauteil / MengeMaterialSpender…" (no visible gaps) to clean spacing; band-row thumbnails no longer overlapped project titles; Bauteilbörsen IDs like "BB-08Materialrest24" (touching) now show a clear gap. The Anforderungsmapping table was checked and did not need the change (wraps cleanly already).

**Two anomalies found and deliberately left untouched** (flagged, not silently fixed — out of scope for a font-size feature): the Quellen table's per-row citation URLs (`\url{...}` after a mid-cell `\\`) still fragment character-by-character regardless of text-size — confirmed identical severity before/after, so it's a separate `\url`/column-width interaction, not a font-size problem.

Verified: rebuilt all 6 print templates (12 PDFs, light+dark) and the full zwischenbericht (light+dark) clean — zero errors, zero unresolved references, confirmed via cropped page renders that the Figure `text-size=12pt` demo (previously a no-op) now visibly enlarges, the new Table `text-size=8pt` demo visibly shrinks, and the Projekte/Bauteilbörsen fixes hold.
